2. What the work reached

The workload held 238.4 units/s for the whole sustained window, against a measured compute roof of 290.0 units/s, which puts it at 82 percent of that roof. The corpus behind those figures is disclosed in section 3 (What was submitted).

Telemetry sat at the configured limit for 401 of 401 busy samples, aggregated across both units, so the configured limit, and not the roof, is the thing to talk about.

3. What was submitted

Inputs were generated from a template whose varying part sits at the head of every input, so no input repeats and no prefix can be reused. Size was requested in requested items per input and counted in items the engine reports having consumed, and every rate here is quoted on the counted basis.

The cache state was read rather than argued. The counter source was the engine's own cache counter, read at the start and the end of the window, it resolved to off, and the reading licenses exactly this: the cache resolved off for the whole window, so no rate reported here was served from it.

What this workload does not establish: these rates are not comparable with any named external suite, because the input distribution is ours and no suite specifies it.
